blocks.title: Why Good Leads {{Never Reach a Rep}}
blocks.description: Inbound demand rarely fails because the offer is wrong. It fails in the gap between the moment someone raises their hand and the moment a person actually reads it - and that gap is where three structural problems compound.

cards.title: Speed Decides Who Wins the Deal
cards.description: Inbound interest decays by the minute. A form fill that waits in a queue until someone opens the CRM has already lost to whoever answered first - the pitch never gets a chance to matter.

cards.title: Reps Spend the Day Sorting, Not Selling
cards.description: Every inbound lead looks identical until a human talks to it. Manual triage burns selling hours on traffic that was never going to buy, while genuinely ready buyers wait in the same undifferentiated queue.

cards.title: Not-Ready Leads Quietly Disappear
cards.description: Most inbound leads are not ready today but will be within a quarter. Without follow-up that someone owns, they sit untouched in the CRM until a competitor re-engages them first.

blocks.title: How the {{Lead Qualification Agent}} Works
blocks.subtitle: Six stages run automatically between the moment a lead arrives and the moment a rep opens a qualified, summarized record.

items.title: The Lead Arrives on Any Channel
items.description: A form fill, web chat, inbound call, WhatsApp message, or email lands and the agent picks it up immediately - no queue, no business hours.

items.title: The Conversation Opens in Seconds
items.description: The agent starts qualifying on the same channel the lead chose, in natural back-and-forth rather than a form.

items.title: Fit Gets Scored in Conversation
items.description: It reasons about need, timing, budget signals, and decision authority from plain answers, then scores the lead against the criteria you define.

items.title: Hot Leads Route to the Right Rep
items.description: Qualified leads reach their owner with the score, the reasoning, and the full transcript while intent is still live.

items.title: The Rest Enter Owned Nurture
items.description: Not-ready leads are tiered instead of dropped, then re-checked over time and escalated the moment the signals change.

items.title: Everything Lands in Your CRM
items.description: Scores, summaries, transcripts, and next steps write back to the record, so pipeline reporting reflects what actually happened.

rows.leftDescription: A lead waits until someone opens the queue - often the next business day for anything that arrives in the evening or over a weekend.
rows.rightDescription: The agent replies on the channel the lead used, at any hour, before attention moves to the next vendor.

rows.leftTitle: Only part of the inbound gets worked
rows.leftDescription: Whatever the team reaches before the next batch arrives gets a conversation; the remainder ages in the CRM.
rows.rightTitle: Every inbound lead gets a conversation
rows.rightDescription: Volume spikes do not change coverage - each lead is qualified as it arrives.

rows.leftDescription: Selling hours go to sorting, chasing, and re-asking the same qualifying questions by hand.
rows.rightTitle: Reps open the day with qualified leads
rows.rightDescription: Scoring, summarizing, and data entry are already done, so rep time goes to conversations that can close.

rows.leftDescription: Only the leads that happen to surface at the top of the queue reach a person while they are still deciding.
rows.rightTitle: Every qualified lead reaches its owner
rows.rightDescription: Routing happens at qualification time, with the context the rep needs to continue the conversation.

rows.leftTitle: The same manual work recurs weekly
rows.leftDescription: Triage, CRM updates, and follow-up sequences are rebuilt by hand every week the team keeps up.
rows.rightTitle: Hours per week return to selling
rows.rightDescription: Qualification, routing, CRM writes, and nurture keep running without a rep touching them.

blocks.title: Put Every Inbound Lead in Front of the {{Right Rep}}
blocks.description: One agent qualifies every inbound lead in conversation, scores it against your criteria, routes the ready ones to their owner with full context, and keeps the rest warm until the timing changes - all synced to your CRM. Start free and have it live in days.

items.question: Which channels can the agent qualify leads across?
items.answer: Web forms and site chat, inbound calls, SMS, WhatsApp, and email. The same qualifying logic runs on every channel, and a lead who switches channels keeps their history and score instead of starting over.

items.question: How does the agent score and tier a lead?
items.answer: It reasons about what it collects in conversation - need, timing, budget signals, and decision authority - against the criteria you define, then assigns a tier. The tier drives whether the lead is routed to a rep now or enters nurture.

items.question: What happens to leads that are not ready to buy?
items.answer: They are tiered as nurture rather than discarded. The agent runs follow-up over time, re-checks readiness in conversation, and escalates to a rep as soon as the signals change.

items.question: How do qualified leads reach our reps?
items.answer: The agent routes each qualified lead to its owner in your CRM with a written summary, the score and the reasoning behind it, and the full conversation history attached, so the rep continues the conversation instead of restarting it.
